 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400, and car bearing No.KA-04-MJ- 6289 alleging that on 02.08.2022 at about 01.40 p.m. when he was standing on the footpath of service road i.e. near Peresandra Cross service road, Chikkaballapura taluk, driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 drove the same negligently from Chikkaballapura side, at the same time, driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 drove the same negligently from Gudibande side, driver of the Lorry dashed the same to the car, then car dashed to the petitioner, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Govt. Hospital, Chikkaballapura, Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the pleadings on 19.06.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 02.08.2022 at about 1.40 p.m., at Peresandra Cross, Chikkaballapura Taluk and District, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the drivers of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-40-5400 and Verna Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MJ-6289 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
3.
What order?
8. On 20.07.2023, 03.08.2023, 15.04.2024 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 11 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.11.
On 05.09.2023, 19.03.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Prakashappa as P.W.2 and get produced 3 documents at Exs.P.12 to 14.

On 04.10.2024 respondent No.1 and 3 insurance companies produced the evidence of officers as R.W.1 and 2 and get produced 3 documents at Exs.R.1 to 3.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.
On 05.12.2024 the counsel for the petitioner filed the written arguments.

10. On the basis of the material record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...Due to the negligent use of Car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 and lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 at the ratio of 50:50 accident taken place, resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Issue No.2 ... Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.26,00,578/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence petitioner/P.W.1 stated that on 02.08.2022 at about 01.40 p.m.
when he was standing on the footpath at Periyasandra Cross on Service Road, Chikkaballapura taluk in order to cross the road, the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 drove the same from Chikkaballapura side negligently, dashed the same to car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 which has been drove negligently from Gudibande side, made the car to dash to the petitioner, thereby caused the accident, resulting in injuries to the petitioner.

sentences.text: In the written statements respondents denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
13. In the cross-examination made on behalf of the respondent No.1, petitioner stated that the accident taken place on the service road, which measuring 30 ft. width.
P.W.1 stated that Dadapeer has filed the complaint about the accident in which his status is noted as standing on the footpath.
P.W.1 submitted that police have seized the lorry and car which are involved in the accident.

P.W.1 submitted that as per the IMV Report, right side doors of the Car are damaged and lorry also damaged.
14.
In the cross-examination made on behalf of the respondent No.3, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that during accident, he was standing on the road and in the place of accident, there is no footpath.
15. In the evidence affidavit P.W.2 Dr. Prakashappa T.H. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

16. In the evidence affidavit RW1/Officer of respondent No.1-Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
R.W.2/Officer of HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co.Ltd., an hear say witnesses of the incident have re-iterated the same facts as narrated in the written statements, which are neither admissible in evidence nor believable.

17. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR registered by Peresandra police pertaining to crime No.157/2022 against the drivers of the lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint filed by Dadapeer, S/o Moulsab.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the complaint dated 02.08.2022.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of wound certificate, which is not properly readable.
Ex.P.5 is the Motor Vehicle Inspection Report pertaining to lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289.

Ex.P.6 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Peresandra police in crime No.157/2022 against Anandkumar, driver of car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 and Muniraju,
S/o. Ganganarasappa, driver of lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of Discharge Summary in which reasons for the injury is noted as hit by the car/four wheeler on 2.8.2022 at 1.30 p.m. near Peresandra bus stand, Chikkaballapura.

18. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records regarding reason,
mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 02.08.2022 at about 01.40 p.m. when petitioner was standing on the footpath at Periyasandra Cross in order to cross the Service Road, Chikkaballapura taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and Car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 at the ratio of 50:50, the lorry dashed to the car, then car dashed to the petitioner, thereby caused accident resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner by analyzing the evidence available in the file requested to award compensation as claimed in the petition by Chand Basha P.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139755693/

20. In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No.1 and 3 by analyzing the evidence available on file, requested to award reasonable compensation.
21. In the light of the submission made on behalf of both the parties with reference to the judgments cited above, I have assessed the compensation.

22. In the evidence affidavit, P.W.1 stated that in the accident, he has suffered post traumatic open left Distal 1/3rd both bones fracture with Type 3-C Open wound with absent peripheral pulses, took first aid treatment at Govt. Hospital, Chikkaballapura, then took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient for a period of 25 days, underwent operation/wound debridement with external fixation, underwent amputation of left leg below knee, took follow up treatment for a period of eight months, at the cost of Rs.6,50,000/-

Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident,
he used to earn Rs.20,000/- p.m. by vending eatables at Bus stand.
23. In the written statements, respondents denied the allegations regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

24. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that if he was earning Rs.20,000/-
p.m., BPL card would not have been issued to him.
Petitioner has not submitted any documents to show that he was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Petitioner admitted that in the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.9, his date of birth is noted as 10.01.1993.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he has not produced document to show that he took treatment by spending Rs.1,00,000/-.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he has not produced any document to show requirement of Rs.5,00,000/- to purchase the artificial limb.
Petitioner stated that in Sanjaygandhi Hospital, he underwent amputation.
25. In the evidence affidavit Dr.Prakashappa stated that on 09.08.2022 under Anaesthesia petitioner underwent amputation of left leg below knee.
P.W.2 stated that on 03.08.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 65% to left lower limb, which is 32.5% to whole body.

In the evidence P.W.2 produced Case sheet,
X-ray and CT scan films at Exs.P.12 to 14.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated that he has treated the petitioner at Sanjay Gandhi hospital.
P.W.2 admitted that the course of treatment is completed.
27. In the evidence R.W.1 and 2 stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

28. Discharge summary, OPD Records, medical bills, prescriptions, case sheet, x-rays and other medical records shows that in the incident petitioner suffered post traumatic open left Distal 1/3rd both bones fracture with Type 3-C open wound with absent peripheral pulses, took treatment at Govt. hospital, Chikkaballapur, then at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 02.08.2022 to 26.08.2022, underwent amputation of left leg below knee by spending approximately Rs.14,578/-.
In the copy Aadhar card date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 10.01.1993.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.

29. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered, length and nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner, I award Rs.5,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.14,578/- towards treatment charges, Rs.50,000/-
towards attendant, conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.1,55,000/- (Rs.15,500 x 10) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.3,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness and Rs.15,81,000/- towards loss of future income (permanent functional disability due to amputation is calculated in the following terms).
Age of the deceased as on the date of 29 years accident:

Monthly income of the petitioner as on the Rs.15,500/- date of accident :
50% Permanent functional disability Rs.7,750/- suffered by the petitioner:
Loss of future income due to permanent Rs.15,81,000/- disability 7750x12x17 30.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.26,00578/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation.

31. In the light of Judgments cited above, considering the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and alleged occupation of the petitioner, I came to the conclusion that compensation assessed at Rs.26,00,578/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. is just, proper and reasonable.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
32. Issue No.3:

Copy of the policies marked at Ex.R.2 and R.3 shows that as on the date of accident Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and Car bearing No.KA-04-MJ- 6289 had insurance coverage with respondent No. 1 and 3 respectively.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondent No.1 and 2 being Insurer and owner of Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and respondent No.3 and 4 being Insurer and owner of car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 are liable to pay compensation at the ratio of 50:50 and award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I Chand Basha P.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139755693/

sentences.text: The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 and 2 being Insurer and owner of Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and respondent No.3 and 4 being Insurer and owner of car bearing No.KA-04-MJ- 6289 shall pay Rs.26,00,578/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to the petitioner towards compensation.

The respondent No.1, being Insurer of Lorry bearing No.KA-40-5400 and respondent No.3 being Insurer of car bearing No.KA-04-MJ-6289 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest at the ratio of 50:50 within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% of compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.

Surplus compensation and interest shall be deposited in any bank in the name of the petitioner for a period of 5 years without permitting to create any encumbrances reserving liberty to withdraw interest once in three months in accordance with law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bangalore.
